title: Guelph's new advocacy plan and CAO objectives
subtitle: Also: council expense policy updates, waste by-law changes for the Blue Box Regulation, staff recognition.
overview: The committee recommended approval of Future in Focus, Guelph's Advocacy Plan. It sets out how the city decides which issues to raise with other governments and which tactics to use. Priorities include housing, infrastructure funding, homelessness and mental health, and employment lands. This should make the city's requests to provincial and federal governments more consistent and easier to follow.

After a closed session on the Chief Administrative Officer's performance review, the committee recommended approving the CAO's 2025 performance objectives {{vote:m2}}. The CAO then presented them in open session, organized around affordability, housing, culture and relationships.

On the consent agenda, the committee recommended amendments to the Waste Management By-law to align with the provincial Blue Box Regulation. It also recommended an updated City Council Expense Policy {{vote:m4}}. Council will consider these recommendations later this month. The committee also recognized a staff member for completing a municipal administration certificate.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving Guelph's advocacy plan, which sets a four-step process for choosing issues and tactics and sets key advocacy directions tied to the strategic plan {{vote:m5}}.
The committee recommended approving the Chief Administrative Officer's 2025 performance objectives and asked that they be presented in open session {{vote:m2}}.
The committee recommended amending the Waste Management By-law to align with the provincial Blue Box Regulation.
The committee recommended approving the updated City Council Expense Policy {{vote:m4}}.

debate: On the expense policy, a councillor asked why town hall materials cannot carry city branding. Staff said it keeps political communications separate from corporate city communications.

Another councillor questioned why mileage and meal rates now point to a separate travel and expense policy. Staff said this avoids updating several policies whenever rates change, and agreed to circulate the amounts before Council considers the item.

On the advocacy plan, councillors asked how water supply advocacy balances growth with conservation. Staff said they mostly use public policy consultations, such as comments on a recent permit to take water.

A councillor asked whether provincial funding wording should refer to Guelph through the county as service manager. Staff said the city often advocates jointly with the county because it does not always know how funding will flow.

Councillors asked about measuring success beyond grants received, and about public reporting. Staff said they will move toward outcome-based measures and add qualitative information in the July performance reporting, and may use the city's public website to show advocacy materials.
